question: The increasing sequence of positive integers \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\) \(\ldots\) has the property that, for every \(n\ge1,\) \[ a_{n+2}=a_n+a_{n+1}. \] If \(a_7=120,\) then \(a_8\) is
solution:
The recurrence determines every term from the first two, so let \(a_1=p\) and \(a_2=q\), where \(p,q\) are integers with \(0<p<q\). Repeated addition gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_3&=p+q,\\
a_4&=p+2q,\\
a_5&=2p+3q,\\
a_6&=3p+5q,\\
a_7&=5p+8q=120.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(5p\) and \(120\) are divisible by \(5\), so is \(8q\). Since \(5\) does not divide \(8\), \(q\) must be a multiple of \(5\). Also, \(p>0\) implies \(8q<120\), so \(q<15\). The only possibilities are therefore \(q=5\) and \(q=10\).

If \(q=5\), the equation gives \(p=16\), contradicting \(p<q\). If \(q=10\), it gives \(p=8\), which is allowed. These two cases exhaust the possibilities.

Starting with \(8,10\), the sequence is
\[8,10,18,28,46,74,120,194,\ldots.\]
It remains positive and increasing because each new term is the sum of two positive terms. Thus \(\boxed{a_8=194}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The recurrence can be reversed by subtracting: \(a_n=a_{n+2}-a_{n+1}\). Let \(t=a_6\), a positive integer, and use \(a_7=120\) to work backward:
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_5&=120-t,\\
a_4&=2t-120,\\
a_3&=240-3t,\\
a_2&=5t-360,\\
a_1&=600-8t.
\end{aligned}
\]
The conditions \(a_1>0\) and \(a_1<a_2\) give
\[t<75,\qquad 600-8t<5t-360.\]
The second inequality simplifies to \(t>960/13\). Since \(13\cdot73=949\) and \(13\cdot74=962\), the only integer satisfying both bounds is \(t=74\).

This yields \(a_1=8\) and \(a_2=10\), which generate the positive increasing sequence \(8,10,18,28,46,74,120,\ldots\), so the candidate satisfies the original conditions. Finally,
\[a_8=a_6+a_7=74+120=\boxed{194}.\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
